## Interface surface

Hermes runs an **OpenAI-compatible API server** exposing `POST /v1/chat/completions`,
plus `/v1/responses` (server-side conversation state), and Runs / Jobs / Sessions
APIs [4]. Any OpenAI-format frontend (Open WebUI, LibreChat, LobeChat, etc.) can
drive it as a backend; the agent runs its full toolset server-side and streams tool
progress inline [4].

## Built-in sandboxing (Hermes' own, distinct from OpenShell)

The landing page advertises "Real Sandboxing" with **five backends — local, Docker,
SSH, Singularity, Modal — with container hardening and namespace isolation** [1].
This is Hermes' *self-contained* isolation for its terminal/code tools. It is process-
and container-level, **not** a kernel-policy sandbox and **not** Kubernetes-native.
NVIDIA OpenShell (see [k3s-openshell-sandboxing.md](k3s-openshell-sandboxing.md)) is a
stricter, external, policy-governed runtime that can wrap Hermes for stronger isolation.

## Gaps and Limitations

- Hermes README/FAQ make **no reference** to OpenShell, NemoClaw, k3s, or Kubernetes
  [5][6]; the k3s + OpenShell composition comes entirely from the NVIDIA side
  (NemoClaw, [10]).
- Exact release date and version history not pinned to a fetched primary.
